The chord goes from y=-14.2 to y=+4.7, so the track crosses the y=0 seam about 17 cm before its end; that matches the mid-track gap and dQ/dx dip near s~20 cm (a break in the 3-D cloud), i.e. the seam was crossed mid-track and the track carries on past it for ~17 cm, so the end itself is not a gap crossing. Profile: plateau ~55k e/cm over 30-70 cm, then a clear climb over the last ~10 cm to ~1.0-1.15e5, following the muon reference curve; the last muon segment 45003 (2.4 cm) averages 106k. No grey continuation past the end in U, V or W of f_meas; the track own cells end cleanly and no dead band sits on the end. Past the stop: one 2.2 cm piece 45001 attached at the stop vertex (d_min 0), leaving at cos_fwd 0.55 (a ~57 deg kink in the c and e azimuths), at 77k (about 1.4x plateau, not several times it, and not straight on), so not a hot-tip undershoot; it reads as a short electron arm and is tagged michel. What made it hard: the Michel is only 2.2 cm, short for a decay electron, so STM_MICHEL vs STM_ONLY rests on that small kinked stub; the stop itself is solid (rise, lower end, seam crossed well before the end).
notes: SEAM: stop is 4.7 cm past the y=0 seam, but the seam is crossed ~17 cm before the end (the s~20 dip) and the end has a real rise, so not a gap crossing. Michel is a 2.2 cm kinked stub, the reason for medium.

evidence: The fit is badly wrong: the real muon is 58010 (151 cm, ~61k), entering through the z=298 side wall (face.z 0.3, x=+261, top volume) and running down to about (168, -169, 187), where the chain then bridges a nearly charge-free, isochronous 114 cm path (58011 4.5k and its twin 58008 8.4k, both at constant x=168 along y) out to the reported stop at y=-305; in f_meas that bridge is only the thin fit line at one time slice (~993) in U and V with no measured charge of its own, and the dQ/dx panel shows it at ~0-20k for s=0-115. So the real end is at arc ~115 cm; dx along 58010 is about -93 of ~150 cm, so it is the lower end, in the top volume, 165 cm above the cathode and 172 cm below the anode. At that real end three short pdg-11 pieces (58006, 58009, 58012; 4-5.5 cm each, 49-64k) drop about 7-10 cm almost vertically (-x) from the junction, a kink of roughly 35-40 deg from the incoming line, seen in all three planes of f_meas as a ~30-slice coloured stub (W channel ~10605, U ~2590, V ~6445) after which the charge ends with no grey carrying either the muon line or the stub on. Before the junction the profile shows only a mild bump (75-95k over s=120-135 against a 50-65k plateau, comparable to scatter further up the track). I read the stub at plateau charge leaving at a kink as the Michel and moved the pin to the junction. What made it hard: the real end sits 0.5-2 cm from the y=-168.5 CRU seam, the stub runs along the seam sheet, the rise is weak, and the ~35-40 deg kink is modest, so a muon scattering at the seam and ending ~10 cm lower (no Michel) or a seam gap crossing into the next CRU (whose channels would fall outside the f_meas window) cannot be excluded; the 3-D stop zooms are centred on the fake end and do not image the real end. Pin arc: the dQ/dx panel origin coincides with context pin (y=-283), from which the ghost runs ~113-115 cm to the real charge; pin_rr 115 is read on that arc.
notes: OVERSHOOT: fit bridges a ~114 cm charge-free isochronous ghost (58011/58008) past the real end; pin moved to the 58010 junction at ~115 cm on the dQ/dx panel arc, bridge tagged delta / other; SEAM: real end 0.5-2 cm from the y=-168.5 CRU seam with only a mild rise; competing readings are a gap crossing (THRU) or a kinked muon end without Michel (STM_ONLY). The 3-D stop frames show the ghost end, not the real end, and f_meas cannot see across the seam into the next CRU channels.
